etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English couple, from Old French couple, from Latin cōpula. Doublet of copula.

definitions.definition: Two of the same kind connected or considered together.

quote.citation: 1692, Roger L'Estrange, Fables, of Aesop and Other Eminent Mythologists: with Morals and Reflexions‎[3], page 64:
quote.text: 'Tis in some sort with Friends (Pardon the Coarseness of the illustration) as it is with Dogs in Couples. They should be of the same Size; and Humour; and That which Pleases the One should Please the Other

quote.citation: 1839, Charles Dickens, Nicholas Nickleby:
quote.text: […] couple of tables; one of which bore some preparations for supper; while, on the other  […]

definitions.definition: Two partners in a romantic or sexual relationship.

quote.citation: 1959, Georgette Heyer, chapter 1, in The Unknown Ajax:
quote.text: And no use for anyone to tell Charles that this was because the Family was in mourning for Mr Granville Darracott […]: Charles might only have been second footman at Darracott Place for a couple of months when that disaster occurred, but no one could gammon him into thinking that my lord cared a spangle for his heir.

definitions.definition: One of the pairs of plates of two metals which compose a voltaic battery, called a voltaic couple or galvanic couple.
(physics) A turning effect created by forces that produce a non-zero external torque.
That which joins or links two things together; a bond or tie; a coupler.

quote.text: As we passed the deserted mountain-dairy, we must have crossed the fresh track of a hare, because the hounds became rather uneasy in the couples.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To join (two things) together, or (one thing) to (another).

quote.citation: 2023 October 28, Leighton Koopman, “YES!!! The Springboks beat the All Blacks to win another Rugby World Cup title”, in Independent Online‎[7]:
quote.text: Some gritty defence at the death, coupled with some key big moments from individual players at critical times helped secure the win as the All Blacks fought with 14 men for a big chunk of the final after a red card to captain Sam Cane.

definitions.definition: (transitive, dated) To join in wedlock; to marry.

quote.citation: 1801, Jonathan Swift, The Works of the Rev. Jonathan Swift, Volume 14‎[8], page 59:
quote.text: I am just going to perform a very good office, it is to assist with the archbishop, in degrading a parson who couples all our beggars

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To join in sexual intercourse; to copulate.

quote.citation: 1987, Alan Norman Bold, Robert Giddings, Who was really who in fiction, Longman:
quote.text: On their wedding night they coupled nine times.

quote.citation: 2001, John Fisher, Geoff Garvey, The rough guide to Crete,, page 405:
quote.text: She had the brilliant inventor and craftsman Daedalus construct her an artificial cow, in which she hid and induced the bull to couple with her [...]

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause (two animals) to copulate, to bring (two animals) together for mating.

quote.citation: 1890, James George Frazer, The Golden Bough, volume 2, page 328:
quote.text: The Parilia was generally considered to be the best time for coupling the rams and the ewes .
